<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**9** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/ai.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/ai.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4443014630c094cde840f9dd0b0b45ade45b48d9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `90a8cf5c8f3e4075eeaebaf31cbf8a92a52596a1` — the merge of head `d80b2d888ddfd4ce5285e4157f645732e1955173` into base `4443014630c094cde840f9dd0b0b45ade45b48d9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 90a8cf5c8f3e4075eeaebaf31cbf8a92a52596a1 && git checkout 90a8cf5c8f3e4075eeaebaf31cbf8a92a52596a1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4443014630c094cde840f9dd0b0b45ade45b48d9 d80b2d888ddfd4ce5285e4157f645732e1955173 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4443014630c094cde840f9dd0b0b45ade45b48d9 && git merge --no-ff d80b2d888ddfd4ce5285e4157f645732e1955173

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4443014630c094cde840f9dd0b0b45ade45b48d9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## L1: ACCEPT · 2026-11-17T21:51Z

Head-sha: d10ea09296e107c40685477e157d64ef8746e1a5
Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c, for card #34918 (os-dev report 6961889053).

### 席位核对

**PR shape.** `Fixes #34918`, base `main`. 13 paths, +372/-16, in two commits:
- `fe96c22d` adds the two shapes in `dataset-tools.zod.ts`, with the tests, the ADR-0149 note and the changeset;
- `d10ea092` regenerates the artefacts.

`'@objectstack/spec': minor` is right, because exports are added. `Clause-②: yes` (a widening) and `Metadata-protocol: added` both match the diff.

**Governed / size.** `check-governed-merges --pr 34982`: GOVERNED, Tier H, on `docs/adr/**`, 388 lines. So the route is the seat's L2, then the Tier H record and os-zhuang.

**CI.** 58 success, 10 expected skips, nothing failed. `Test Core (10/10)` is still running its re-run. This verdict holds on the condition that `Test Core (10/10)` finishes green on this head.

**(a) Describe text says what each slot is (M1).** Every new `describe` names a finding or a slot, and none tells a model what to do:
- `decision` names the four cases by what the platform found (one measure, several measures, candidates only, no measure), and says what each rests on (`matches` or `candidates`);
- `note` and `sourceLine` each say what the string is, that the executor writes it, and that the schema fixes no text.

The ADR note says the same in its second bullet: what follows from each case "stays D3's to say, in the three places D3 names". The note changes no word of M1, of its option table or of its Ruled A line, and the diff confirms it: the ADR change is 11 added lines, all inside the new note.

**(b) Regenerated artefacts, pin and strictness rows.** Each count follows from the zod change:
- **`references/index.mdx`**: AI 82 → 84 schemas, total 1670 → 1672, and the `dataset-tools.zod.ts` row gains `DatasetNextStep` and `DatasetNextStepDecision`. Two new exported schemas, two new rows.
- **`api-surface`**: the four entries are the const and type for each of the two.
- **`authorable-surface`**: `DatasetNextStep:{decision,note,terms}`, `ListDatasetsOutput:nextStep` and `QueryDatasetOutput:sourceLine`. That is five keys, which is exactly the diff.
- **`json-schema.manifest`**: the same two schemas. `declaration-map` and `export-origins` gain three lines each, consistent with that.
- **Type-alias pin**: 858 → 860, with two `Iso_` pins, one for the enum and one for the object, and both header numbers moved together. Neither shape has a default or a transform, so `z.input` equals `z.infer`, as the pin claims.
- **Strictness ledger**: `ai/` 97 → 98. That is one new `z.object` site (`DatasetNextStepSchema`). The `ListDatasetsOutput` and `QueryDatasetOutput` changes extend existing sites.

**(c) The terms-reference form against the ruling's "the candidates".** Ruling record 6953671481 says `nextStep` carries "a closed decision, the candidates, a sentence". The PR carries the candidates by reference: `terms` names the caller's terms, and the members are read under those terms from the same answer's `matches` and `candidates`. The tests pin that a member list written inside `nextStep` is stripped on parse. This is a strict refinement of the ruled wording, not a different result. Every candidate the ruling meant is reachable, from one list instead of two. The ADR note's "One list of candidates" bullet says so, with the reason (no pointer declared twice). The seat's L2 should state that reading, as it did for #34828 (N1).

**The REST door.** The test pins that `sourceLine` lives only on the tool's output, and that `AnalyticsResultResponseSchema` (the REST data) does not keep it. That is right: the extension sits on `QueryDatasetOutputSchema` alone, and the REST schema is untouched in the diff.

**Value to a customer agent.** After #34919, a client reads the case and a finished sentence from the answer instead of working them out of `matches` and `candidates`. Both clients, the product agent and any MCP client, get the same words.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
- N1. **Mixed cases in one answer.** `nextStep` is one object. If the caller sends two terms in different cases (one equals a measure, another has only candidates), one answer reports one case. The docblock leaves "which case one answer reports" to the executor. The singular object follows the ruled wording ("a closed decision"), and `matches` and `candidates` still carry every term, so no data is lost. But the precedence is a contract readers will depend on. #34919 should state and pin it, for example that a case that asks goes before one that computes. If the seat's L2 wants the shape itself to be per-term (an array), that has to be decided before this lands, because changing an object to an array later is breaking.
- N2. The ADR note's header reads "— this PR". The seat's L2 on #34928 (N3) preferred "PR #N". Fold that in only if there is another push anyway.

Next: the seat's L2 (Tier H, an ADR-0149 amendment note and new spec shapes), then the Tier H record and os-zhuang. A later push owes an L1-c delta read.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d10ea09296e107c40685477e157d64ef8746e1a5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/dataset-tools.zod.ts, docs/adr/0149-ai-answers-business-questions-through-the-dataset-semantic-layer.md + none
Security-touching: no

**This record covers `d10ea09296` only. The PR head moved to `d304f1b861` at 21:59Z while this review ran** (one commit on top, 9 changed lines in the two `hits` files: the `DatasetNextStepSchema` doc comment and the ADR note's header). That head and anything after it are the seat's separate delta and are not judged here.

Read for this record: card #34918 (body and all four comments: triage 6954733026 and 6959430017, claim 6959561891, os-dev report 6961889053), ruling record 6953671481 on #34894, the body of #34919 (the first consumer, where the ruling's four-way sentence is quoted), PR #34982 (body, the 13-file list, the three comments including L1-c 6962024627, and the net diff from merge-base `44c7a4a415` to the head), contract record 6948719696 on #34828 (for its N1 form), and the check-runs on the head. Nothing was built or run. Read but not reviewed, outside the diff: `packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-tools.ts` (identical at the head and on `origin/main` `db1a05cdae`), `packages/spec/liveness/README.md` and `packages/spec/liveness/dataset.json`. `+ none`: no file in the diff implements or enforces the two `hits` files apart from tests and generator output, which are the lane seat's remainder; the executor is #34919 and is not in this diff. Not read: the hosted wrapper (cloud `53a5844`); every statement about it below rests on the two cards' quoted evidence.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set of `ListDatasetsOutputSchema`: widened by one optional key. Right.** An answer without `nextStep` parses to the same value as before. An answer with `{ decision, terms, note }` is now kept, where the plain `z.object` dropped the unknown key before.
- **Accept-set of `QueryDatasetOutputSchema`: widened by one optional key. Right.** `sourceLine` is declared in the tool's own `.extend()`; `AnalyticsResultResponseSchema` is not edited in the diff, so the REST answer is what it was.
- **Two narrow refusals are new, and they are right.** A malformed `nextStep` (a fifth `decision` value, empty `terms`, empty `note`, a missing member) and an empty-string `sourceLine` parsed before (the key was dropped) and are refused now. No producer in this repository emits either key: `dataset-tools.ts` at the head returns `datasets`, `partial`, `warning`, `candidates` only. The one known producer is outside it, the hosted wrapper; see ③.
- **Public surface: four new exports from `@objectstack/spec/ai`. Right.** `DatasetNextStepSchema`, `DatasetNextStepDecision` (const and type), `DatasetNextStep` (type). Nothing is removed or renamed.
- **The generated surfaces agree with the zod, line by line.** api-surface +4 (the four exports). export-origins +3 and declaration-map +3 (three names; the enum's const and type share one). json-schema.manifest +2 (`ai/DatasetNextStep`, `ai/DatasetNextStepDecision`). authorable-surface +5 (`DatasetNextStep:decision`, `:note`, `:terms`, `ListDatasetsOutput:nextStep`, `QueryDatasetOutput:sourceLine`); `authorable-surface.base.json` did not move. Strictness count `ai/` 97 to 98 (one new `z.object` site; the two output schemas are existing sites). Pin count 858 to 860 with two `Iso_` rows; neither schema has a default or a transform. Reference totals 1670 to 1672, AI 82 to 84. `references/ai/dataset-tools.mdx` carries the three `describe` strings and the `sourceLine` string byte for byte, the four enum values in declaration order, `nextStep` and `sourceLine` as optional, and the module text as rewritten.
- **MCP `outputSchema` of both tools gains the member from this PR on, before anything fills it. Right, and stated** (changeset, ADR note's last bullet, PR body). The projected `nextStep` is closed (`additionalProperties: false`, three required members), pinned by a test in the diff.
- **`matches`, `candidates`, `provenance`, the input schemas and normalization: untouched.** Confirmed in the diff.
- **Gate verdicts, read off the check-runs on `d10ea09296` as they stood at 22:00Z, after the push of `d304f1b861`.** 70 check-runs: 59 success, 10 skipped, 1 cancelled, none pending.
  - Success, among the 59: `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Lint & Repo Gates` and its eight `Lint ·` jobs, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Test UI` and its 16 shards, `Test Core (1/10)` to `(9/10)`.
  - **`Test Core (10/10)` has no green conclusion on this head, and now cannot get one.** Attempt 1 (job 134374463545) concluded failure: per the dev report, `plugin-hono-server` `adapter-drain.test.ts`, the idle keep-alive case. Attempt 2 (job 134393738065) was cancelled at 21:59:26Z, annotation "Canceling since a higher priority waiting request for ci-CI-pull_request-34982 exists": the push of `d304f1b861` superseded run 44177643620. Superseded, not settled. The diff holds no file under `packages/plugins/**` and the failing file names nothing from spec, but that is a reading of the diff, not a gate verdict: the shard's green is owed by the check-runs of the final head, and the delta record reads it there.
  - The roll-up `Test Core` of attempt 2 (job 134400799137) reads success although its tenth shard was cancelled. It is not counted as a verdict on the tenth shard here.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` at `minor`, one changeset, no other package. That matches what the diff publishes: four additive exports and two optional output members, nothing removed or renamed. `Check Changeset` is success on the head.

Clause-②: yes (widening: two optional output members on published schemas). The line is the same in the PR body, the changeset and the claim, and it is correct: the only narrowing is the refusal of a malformed value under two keys no in-repo producer writes.

`Metadata-protocol: added` is right. The authorable-surface baseline gains five rows, and the level gate that reads the line is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question 1 (one `nextStep` or one per term): seat ruling A is sound. Not escalated.** The ruling record says "a closed decision", singular, and #34919's acceptance is four single-word calls, each returning one decision. Nothing in the ruling's text requires a per-term list. An answer with terms in different cases loses no data: `matches` and `candidates` carry every term, and `nextStep.terms` says which terms the reported case covers. The fear behind the question, that an object cannot become a list later, does not force a list now: a later optional sibling or an optional member inside `nextStep` is additive. One condition goes to #34919 with this answer, N1 below.
- **Open question 2 (the four values): seat ruling A is sound. Not escalated.** The mapping to the ruling's four-way sentence as #34919 quotes it: "one match answers" is `one_measure`; "several ask" is `several_measures`; "near ones are offered" is `candidates_only`; "none falls back and says so" is `no_measure`. The four are exhaustive and exclusive per term, given the invariant `candidates` already declares (a term with a match has no candidate): the term equals one measure, or more than one, or no measure with candidates, or no measure without. The card's evidence about the wrapper ("a closed decision, the candidates and a finished sentence"; computed "from the framework's own matches") names no fifth case. The wrapper's own value names were not readable by the dev, the seat or this review; if they differ, the difference is in spelling, which the cloud PR that removes the wrapper absorbs.
- **Dev deviation, the hosted wrapper not measured:** accepted; see the line above.
- **Declared but not yet produced: acceptable under the repo's liveness rules.** The liveness ledger governs authorable metadata; its README classes a computed projection as `output`, "Not authorable". `packages/spec/liveness/` has no row for the dataset-tools output schemas and gains none in this diff, and `Spec property liveness` is success on the head. ADR-0049's enforce-or-remove is about a key an author can write and nothing reads; these two members are written by the server. The pending half is named by card (#34919) in the ADR note's last bullet, the changeset and the module doc, which is ADR-0149 D6's form and the form `candidates` landed in (#34828, filled by #34763). No strictness-ledger verdict row is owed: the count file moved by the one new object site and its gate is green.
- **The hosted wrapper is a second producer of both key names until cloud removes it** (ruling record: "The hosted wrapper is removed and reads the framework's"; #34690). From this PR on, a spec parse of a wrapper-shaped `nextStep` that is not `{ decision, terms, note }` with these four values is refused, and the projected `outputSchema` describes this shape. Cloud's spec bump and the wrapper's removal belong in one change. Carrier: the cloud PM, through #34690. Not a defect of this head.
- **`Skills-docs: follow-up owed`** names `skills/objectstack-ask/SKILL.md` and no card number. The PR-body guard is green; the seat owes the number before landing, as on #34828.
- **Known overlaps** with #34925 and #34719 (the pin count, the generated index totals): a merge-order matter, stated in the PR body with the remedy.
- **SQL push-down:** not applicable. The diff holds a schema, prose, tests and generator output; it adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.
- **Security-touching is `no`.** No changed hunk states permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour. The nearest sentence is "computed by the platform from this answer's `matches` and `candidates`", which says what the member is computed from. It has a consequence #34919 must hold, N5 below. The PR is Tier H in any case (`docs/adr/**` and `packages/spec/**`).

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`packages/spec/src/ai/dataset-tools.zod.ts`, against the ruling, ADR-0149 D3 and its first consumer.**

- The enum counts measures, and that agrees with the code that carries D3 to a model today. `LIST_DATASETS_DESCRIPTION` on `main` (`dataset-tools.ts:85-99`) reads: a word "that matches exactly one measure wins"; "One word matching several measures (in one dataset or two): ask"; a word that matched nothing may have `candidates`; "No match and no candidates: fall back"; "A dimension match alone picks a grouping, not a number". The four values are those four sentences as findings, in the same grain.
- Every `describe` states a fact and none instructs a model, which is what M1 A asks. `note` and `sourceLine` fix no wording, template or language.
- `terms` is a sound join key. Every `matches` entry and every `candidates` entry carries the caller's term as sent, and the description says which list to read for which case, including that only entries whose `member` is a measure count for the two measure cases.
- `sourceLine` beside `provenance` holds: optional, non-empty, absence is the one spelling of "none", and the REST shape is not widened.
- I tried to break it on seven cases. None breaks the declared shape; three leave a duty with #34919 (N1, N2, N5).
  1. Two terms, each equal to one different measure: `one_measure` with both terms. The description on `main` says "two such words are two metrics, so compute both". Expressible.
  2. One term equal to the same-named measure in two datasets: `several_measures`, D3 rule 3. Expressible.
  3. A term equal to one measure and one dimension: `one_measure`, because a dimension is not counted. See N3.
  4. A measure word with a dimension word, the input schema's own example `["营收", "销售阶段"]`: see N1.
  5. A term whose only equal member is withheld from this caller: it has no match in the answer, so the case computed from the answer is `candidates_only` or `no_measure`, and nothing withheld is named, provided the sentence is composed from the answer too (N5).
  6. A degraded answer (`partial: true`): see N4.
  7. A client on an older spec: the plain `z.object` drops the unknown key, no failure.

**The by-term reading of the ruling's "the candidates", stated so that nobody has to infer it.** Ruling record 6953671481 lists what `nextStep` holds as "a closed decision, the candidates, a sentence". The shape holds `decision`, `terms`, `note`. It lists no member. "The candidates" are carried by reference: for each term in `nextStep.terms`, they are the entries carrying that term in the same answer, the measure entries of the datasets' `matches` for `one_measure` and `several_measures`, and the entries of `candidates` for `candidates_only`. This is within the ruling. Every member the ruling meant is in the answer, it is found by an exact string comparison on a key both lists already carry, and it exists once, so there is no second list that could disagree with the first (the card's own scope line: "does not declare the same list twice"). Two things the reference cannot say. It cannot name a subset: a term in `terms` refers to all of its entries, never to some of them. And it does not hand the reader the candidates ready to read, only where they are; N2 says why that matters and who carries it. 一句话：裁决记录写的是「一个封闭的判断、候选项、一句话」，实际形状是「判断 + 所指的词 + 一句话」；候选项不在 `nextStep` 里重复列出，而是按词到同一份返回的 `matches` 和 `candidates` 里去读。裁决所指的每个候选都读得到，而且全篇只有一份，所以仍在裁决范围内。表达不了的只有两点：不能只指其中几条，以及候选不是现成摆在 `nextStep` 里的，要靠那句成文的话把它们写出来。

**N1 (nit) — a term that equals only a dimension is `no_measure`, the same value as an unknown word, and the commonest call mixes it with a measure word.** The enum's doc comment puts a dimension-only term in `no_measure` (rule 5) and defines `no_measure` by rule 4. Rule 5 is about a question with no measure hit at all, not about one term. The input schema's own example, `["营收", "销售阶段"]`, is by this per-term definition already a mixed call: one term in `one_measure`, one in `no_measure`. The declared shape expresses the right answer (`one_measure`, `terms: ["营收"]`, with the dimension match left in `matches`), and no declared sentence is false, so this does not block the head. But a precedence in #34919 that puts every non-computing case first, which L1-c offers as an example, would report "no measure" for the commonest ask-data question. #34919 must state and pin that a dimension-matched term never outranks a measure-matched one, and what the answer reports when the only term sent equals a dimension. If the seat would rather publish a fifth value for the dimension-only case, that is free before merge and a breaking change for exhaustive readers after; I do not ask for it: the finding "no measure" is true in both cases, the ruling names four, and `matches` tells the two apart. Carrier: #34919.

**N2 (nit) — the by-term reference leaves the candidates for the reader to assemble unless `note` names them.** #34919's evidence records the wrapper's measured reason for a finished string: a model handed one copies it, and one that assembles it from parts often does not. With no member list inside `nextStep`, the finished-string property rests on `note` alone. For `several_measures` and `candidates_only`, #34919's sentence should name each offered member by label and dataset label (D3 rule 3's listing), with a pin. Should measurement show that models still fail to gather them, an optional member list inside `nextStep` can be added later without breaking a reader. Carrier: #34919.
